# ServanaGo

> Lightweight self-hosted web runtime manager: a Go app with a web UI, embedded Caddy, SQLite and (planned) systemd integration. Status: early. The code is still the inherited baseline, a single-process Caddy front end that publishes reverse-proxy routes under domains, with optional Cloudflare integration (DNS-01 certificates and A records). Static sites, Node.js and PHP-FPM runtimes, systemd supervision and native packaging are planned (see docs/ROADMAP.md), not shipped. MIT licensed.

Target platform: native host, Debian 12+ / Ubuntu 22.04+ with systemd. There is no container image and no package yet; run it from source.

## Run from source

Prerequisites: Go and a domain. Cloudflare is optional: with a Cloudflare API token (`Zone:Zone:Read` and `Zone:DNS:Edit`) ServanaGo uses DNS-01 certificates (wildcards available) and manages A records; without one it uses per-host HTTP-01/TLS-ALPN certificates (ports 80 and 443 reachable from the internet), manages no DNS, and each domain is added by hand on the Domains page. A record targets can be any usable IPv4 (public, private or CGNAT); loopback, link-local, multicast and reserved addresses are refused. IPv6 is dual-stack: an optional IPv6 address beside each IPv4 one adds an AAAA record (IPv4 stays required; no IPv6-only sites).

1. `make build` produces `bin/servanago`.
2. `cp .env.example .env` and fill it in. Required: `SERVANAGO_HOST` (hostname for the UI), `ACME_EMAIL` (bare address). Optional Cloudflare: `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN`, which then also requires `SERVANAGO_HOST_IP` (private IPv4 the host resolves to). Set `ADMIN_PASSWORD`: it creates the first administrator (`ADMIN_USER`, default `admin`) on first start; with no administrator the UI is open.
3. ServanaGo reads the process environment only; export the file (`set -a; . ./.env; set +a`) and run `DATA_DIR="$PWD/data" ./bin/servanago` as an unprivileged user. To bind 80/443: `sudo setcap cap_net_bind_service=+ep bin/servanago`, or set `HTTP_PORT` and `HTTPS_PORT`.
4. Open `https://<SERVANAGO_HOST>` and log in. ServanaGo creates the `SERVANAGO_HOST` A record itself.

Startup fails fast naming the missing or invalid variable. Set `ACME_STAGING=true` to avoid Let's Encrypt rate limits.

## Configure

Environment variables (secrets are read from the environment only, never stored in SQLite or logs):

- `SERVANAGO_HOST`, `ACME_EMAIL`: required.
- `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` (optional), `SERVANAGO_HOST_IP` (required with a token), `SERVANAGO_HOST_IP6` (optional AAAA target for the host).
- `SERVANAGO_STATIC_ROOTS`: optional colon-separated prefixes a static site's folder must sit under (default: any folder outside `DATA_DIR`, `/etc`, `/proc`, `/sys`, `/dev`, `/root`, `/`).
- `SERVANAGO_HOST_ZONE`: Cloudflare zone of the host; set it if zone auto-detection fails.
- `ADMIN_PASSWORD` + optional `ADMIN_USER`: create the first administrator once, then are ignored (administrators live in the DB: Users page, equal powers, each with their own password, authenticator, backup codes and passkeys; every action is on the Audit page). `SERVANAGO_SECRET_KEY` (32+ chars) enables the authenticator app; `REQUIRE_2FA` enforces it for everyone; `TURNSTILE_SITE_KEY` + `TURNSTILE_SECRET` add Turnstile to the password form.
- Email for the optional magic-link site gate is set per site in the site's form (SMTP or Postmark API token, sender), not in env. The credential is stored sealed with `SERVANAGO_SECRET_KEY`. Links open on `ml.<main hostname>`, created in Cloudflare, so gating needs Cloudflare. The Settings page SMTP account is only for ServanaGo's own notices.
- `ACME_STAGING`, `ACME_ISSUER` (`internal` = self-signed), `ACME_PROPAGATION_DELAY` / `ACME_PROPAGATION_TIMEOUT` (`2m` / `10m` fixes "timed out waiting for record to fully propagate"), `ACME_RESOLVERS` (default `1.1.1.1,8.8.8.8`).
- `UI_LISTEN` (default `127.0.0.1:8080`), `DATA_DIR` (default `/data`, a container-era default; set it explicitly), `HTTP_PORT` / `HTTPS_PORT` (default 80/443).

## Use

All management is through the web UI (htmx, server-rendered); there is no public REST API.

- Add a site: `/sites/new`. Enter one or more hostnames (`oc.example.com`, one per line, first is the main one), choose Proxy (backend host or IP and port as separate fields) or Static (a folder to serve). With Cloudflare, ServanaGo finds the zone for the main hostname, adds the domain if new, and creates the A record; a hostname with no domain is still served (HTTP-01 certificate) and you point DNS at the server yourself. Equivalent to the Caddyfile `oc.example.com { reverse_proxy http://192.168.25.165:9200 }` or `file_server`.
- Domains: `/domains`. Per domain, `cert_mode` is `wildcard` (default) or `per_host`; `default_ip` is where its A records point.
- Sites: `/sites/{id}`. Hostnames, proxy or static kind, enable/disable, CIDR allowlist, basic auth, streaming, upload limit, per-site DNS record IP (applies to every hostname), optional magic-link gate. With Cloudflare each hostname that falls under a managed domain gets its own A (and AAAA) record; dropping a hostname deletes the record ServanaGo created for it.
- Dashboard `/`: upstream health, certificate expiry, DNS state, UI host record card. `/logs`: live Caddy/ACME log. `/help`: plain-language help. `/security`: authenticator app, passkeys, gate identities.
- If the UI host's A record already exists with a different value, the dashboard shows a conflict; nothing is overwritten until you click *Take over*.

## Behavior and constraints

- Every change writes SQLite, renders the full Caddy JSON, then calls `caddy.Load`. If Caddy rejects it, the DB change is reverted and the exact error is shown. If stored config fails to load at startup, a bootstrap config (UI only) is served with a banner.
- Only Cloudflare records marked `managed by servanago` are changed or deleted. Records are DNS-only (never proxied); A targets are IPv4, with an optional IPv6 AAAA target beside each.
- Rejected domains: `.local`, `.internal`, `.home.arpa`, IP literals (Caddy would use its internal CA instead of ACME). A route cannot use the `SERVANAGO_HOST` hostname.
- Backups: the Backups page schedules encrypted archives of the panel and of opted-in sites (files, database dumps, container volumes) and restores a site from them; MCP has `backup_status`, `list_backups`, `run_backup`, `plan_restore`, `restore_site`. The panel is restored only on the server: `servanago backup restore --panel ARCHIVE` with the service stopped. By hand: copy `DATA_DIR` (SQLite DB and Caddy certificate storage). Locked out: another administrator resets you on the Users page, or on the server run `servanago user passwd NAME` (set a password), `servanago user add NAME` (new administrator) or `servanago 2fa-reset NAME` (remove that person's authenticator, backup codes and passkeys); they need only `DATA_DIR`.
- `UI_LISTEN=0.0.0.0:8080` is a recovery hatch only: the UI is then served without TLS.

## Troubleshooting

- "permission denied" on the data directory: it must be writable by the user running ServanaGo.
- Cert never issues: check token scopes, set the propagation variables above, try `ACME_STAGING=true`.
- `expected 1 zone, got 0`: leave `ACME_RESOLVERS` at its default or set `SERVANAGO_HOST_ZONE`.

## Development

- `make test` (`go test -race ./cmd/... ./internal/...`), `make lint`, `make e2e` (Playwright, needs bun and chromium), `make check` (all), `make build`.
- Stack: Go, embedded Caddy with `caddy-dns/cloudflare`, SQLite, Go templates + htmx via `embed.FS`, no Node build step.
